cancho.title: A leaked file, refused by name

steps.note: It opens a file and never closes it. The compiler refuses:
The refusal is data an agent can match on:
One added line fixes it, and the program may now run:
steps.cmd: diff leak.cho fixed.cho; cancho build fixed.cho --std -o notes && ./notes

steps.note: What may it do? The types say:
steps.out:
performs
    fs_read("/tmp")
    io_write
never touches
    the network
    the heap
    the command line
    signals
    other programs
    foreign code

cancho-ui.title: A component that asks for the clock

steps.note: Delete `requires Clock;` and the compiler refuses:
steps.out:
error[capability-missing] at clock_bad.cui:15:21: component `Clock` performs `clock.now` which requires the `Clock` capability, but `requires Clock` is not declared
exit 1

steps.note: With the declaration it is accepted:
Ask what it may reach, as data:
steps.cmd: cancho-ui inspect effects clock.cui Clock | grep '"capability"'

trail:shop-energy.title: A shop's energy, passed between roles
trail:shop-energy.summary: A data scientist, a statistician and a data engineer pass one file between them, each with their own command line. No glue, no new package: a tool that dislikes the file says why, by rule.
trail:shop-energy.source: A recorded run of the real tools, replayed, on synthetic data (shop-energy/make_data.py): nothing here measures a real shop.

steps.note: Data scientist (ml): I take the file as it came. The tool refuses, and names the row and the rule.
steps.cmd: ml fit --model linear --target kwh --output kwh.ml shop.csv | jq -c '.error | {rule, detail}'

steps.note: Statistician (stats): What is wrong with it? Three cells are missing in the target.
steps.cmd: stats describe shop.csv --cols kwh | jq -c '.data.columns[] | {name, count, missing, mean}'

steps.note: Data engineer (table): I drop the rows with no reading, and hand the rest on.
steps.cmd: table --where "kwh != ''" --format csv shop.csv > clean.csv; tail -n +2 clean.csv | wc -l

steps.note: Statistician (stats): Same question on the clean file: exact figures, with the quantiles.
steps.cmd: stats describe clean.csv --cols kwh,outside_c | jq -c '.data.columns[] | {name, count, missing, mean, sd, median: .quantiles[2].value}'

steps.note: Data scientist (ml): Now it fits, and it holds 20% of the rows out to score on.
steps.cmd: ml fit --model linear --target kwh --split train=0.8 --seed 1 --output kwh.ml clean.csv | jq -c '.data.summary | {coefficients: [.coefficients[] | {(.name): .value}], holdout: .holdout.metrics}'

steps.note: Reviewer: Before this ships: what may each tool do? The compilers proved it.
steps.cmd: for t in table stats ml; do echo "$t $($t introspect | jq -c '.authority.effects')"; done
